stem: Ravi starts facing North. He turns 90 degrees clockwise. Which direction is he now facing?

per_option_rationale.rationale: From North, a 90-degree clockwise turn lands on East. Clockwise from N goes N->E->S->W.
West is a 90-degree anticlockwise turn from North, not clockwise.
South is a 180-degree turn from North, not a 90-degree clockwise turn.
Returning to North would require a 360-degree full rotation, not 90 degrees.

explanation: Clockwise rotation from North: 90 degrees -> East, 180 degrees -> South, 270 degrees -> West, 360 degrees -> North. One 90-degree clockwise turn from North lands on East.

explanation_sections.punchline: Clockwise means N->E->S->W; one quarter-turn from North reaches East.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: label the four cardinal directions in clockwise order N-E-S-W. One 90-degree clockwise step advances by one position, giving East.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always apply the clockwise/anticlockwise label before turning: clockwise is N->E->S->W, anticlockwise is N->W->S->E.
explanation_sections.timing: 10-15 seconds. The trap is confusing clockwise with anticlockwise, which gives West instead of East.
